title: Normalized proper/open calculus on strict pro-etale towers
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring and, for every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use the constant ring sheaf $\underline B_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_T))$, with strict inverse systems and module sheaves as in [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal T_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. These tower categories are the module categories on the diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. For a scheme map $u$ let $G_u=u^{-1}$ act termwise, with the canonical constant-ring identifications, and let $R_u^{\mathcal T}$ be total right derived termwise direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Use $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$ with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, and the exact open extension $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied termwise. Mates and composition adjunctions have the normalization of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].
For a cartesian open square $(j:V\hookrightarrow T,j':V'\hookrightarrow T',g:T'\to T,g_V:V'\to V)$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], there is a canonical isomorphism on these derived tower categories
$$\beta_{j,g}:G_gj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!G_{g_V}.$$
Its inverse is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose of the open-extension unit $G_{g_V}M\to G_{g_V}j^{-1}j_!M\cong j'^{-1}G_gj_!M$. It is natural, equals the identity for identity base changes, and its successive-base-change composite equals the comparison for the composite, with the canonical pullback compositors. It also commutes with composition of open immersions. Evaluation on a finite constant coefficient object is the comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. These assertions hold for arbitrary $B$, including infinite $B$.
Consider a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc} V&\xrightarrow{k}&W\\
r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
S&\xrightarrow{i}&T\end{array}$$
with $p,r$ proper and $k,i$ quasi-compact open [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No cartesian hypothesis and no chosen factorization of the square are imposed. Put $W_S=W\times_TS$ with projections $b:W_S\to W$ and $q:W_S\to S$, and let $s=(k,r):V\to W_S$ be the induced map [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $s$ is a clopen immersion: it is open and closed, $bs=k$ and $qs=r$; thus $W_S=s(V)\amalg(W_S\setminus s(V))$ is a decomposition into open subschemes. Here clopen means an open immersion which is also a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$ for the natural projection which is identity on $s(V)$ and zero on its complementary open component. It acts termwise on strict towers and complexes. Define
$$\alpha_Q:G_pi_!\xrightarrow{\beta_{i,p}}b_!G_q\xrightarrow{b_!\pi_sG_q}b_!s_!s^{-1}G_q\cong k_!G_r.$$
In a cartesian square $s$ is the identity and $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$. In a refinement square $V=S$, $r=1_S$, it is projection onto the clopen section $(k,1_S)$. For every commutative proper/open square above, define the normalized proper/open comparison to be the proper-adjunction mate
$$\gamma_Q=(R_p^{\mathcal T}k_!\varepsilon_r)\circ(R_p^{\mathcal T}\alpha_QR_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\eta_pi_!R_r^{\mathcal T}):i_!R_r^{\mathcal T}\longrightarrow R_p^{\mathcal T}k_!.$$
All these are transformations in the derived categories of strict towers. Write $\nu_V:V_{\mathrm{proet}}\to V_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $M\in D(\mathcal T_V)$, suppose each $\operatorname{ev}_n M$ is the restriction of scalars, along a ring homomorphism $B\to\Lambda_n$ with $\Lambda_n$ finite commutative, of $\nu_V^*L_n$ for some $L_n\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $\gamma_{Q,M}$ is an isomorphism. Under the canonical direct-image and open etale/pro-etale comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], its $n$-th evaluation is precisely the normalized finite proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], including its refinement normalization. No uniform lower bound in $n$ is required.
The following identities hold as actual derived strict-tower transformations, for these squares and their horizontal or vertical pastings, with the canonical direct-image, pullback and open-extension composition identifications. For a pasted square use the mate of the pasted $\alpha$ with the composition adjunctions. For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ with left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, right proper maps $p_1,p_2$ and middle open $i_1$,
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}R_{r_1}^{\mathcal T}).$$
For horizontally adjacent squares $Q_1,Q_2$ with top opens $k,l$, bottom opens $i,j$ and proper verticals $r,p,q$,
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\gamma_{Q_2}k_!)\circ(j_!\gamma_{Q_1}).$$
For a base change $b:T_1\to T$, with projections $a:W_1\to W$, $c:S_1\to S$, $d:V_1\to V$ and induced square $Q_1$, let $E_p^{\mathcal T},E_r^{\mathcal T}$ be the mates of the pullback squares. Then
$$(R_{p_1}^{\mathcal T}\beta_k)\circ(E_p^{\mathcal T}k_!)\circ(G_b\gamma_Q)=(\gamma_{Q_1}G_d)\circ(i_{1!}E_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\beta_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
The comparisons for pasted squares use the intrinsic clopen-projection construction just specified; their alpha maps agree with the pasted alpha maps, with the canonical inverse-image and open-extension composition identifications. Thus the two displayed composition laws apply to every commutative proper/open square, including squares between intermediate open schemes in refinements of compatible composition towers, without a cartesian or identity-left hypothesis. The comparisons are independent of parenthesization. Squares with identity vertical maps give the identity on open extension, and squares with identity horizontal maps give the identity on derived direct image. All these equalities hold before evaluation; the evaluation functors are not assumed faithful.

The source states the etale result; the tower realization, finite-evaluation normalization and pro-etale extension are additional assertions to be proved, not quotations from the source.

proof.text: First establish the operations on the whole strict diagram category, without a finiteness assumption on $B$. The canonical constant-ring identifications hold for any ring: the sheafification universal property identifies maps from $\underline B$ to a ring sheaf $F$ with ring maps $B\to F(1)$; composing inverse images of topoi therefore identifies inverse image of $\underline B$ with $\underline B$, preserving its constant sections. Under this identification the module pullback is the exact inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Extension along an open is the localized-site functor of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], by weakly-etale localization. Apply these additive functors termwise to towers. Kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise, so their exactness persists; the componentwise units and counits commute with transitions and give the termwise adjunctions. The diagram-site realization is a small ringed site, so its module complexes admit K-injective resolutions. The right adjoint of an exact additive functor preserves K-injectives. Consequently termwise direct image has its unbounded total derived functor; the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories and the canonical derived-adjunction theorem give $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Exact open extension and open restriction descend directly, giving $j_!\dashv G_j$ with their termwise units and counits. In particular no replacement of strict towers by arbitrary diagrams in individual derived categories has occurred.

proof.text: For the cartesian open square, localization gives $j^{-1}g_*\cong(g_V)_*j'^{-1}$, with the identity comparison on the same sections over the pulled-back test object. Hence $G_gj_!$ and $j'_!G_{g_V}$ are left adjoints of canonically identified right adjoints. The unit-normalized uniqueness of left adjoints supplies their canonical isomorphism $\beta$. Its inverse $t:j'_!G_{g_V}\to G_gj_!$ has $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose equal to $G_{g_V}\eta_j$, followed by $G_{g_V}G_j\cong G_{j'}G_g$: this follows by composing the two adjunction Hom bijections and inserting the open unit. It is the inverse direction specified in the statement. The identities $j^{-1}j_!\cong1$ used here follow directly on the localized extension presheaf: for an object over the open there is exactly one lift to that open. These comparisons, units and their equations act termwise on towers and complexes, and descend by exact-functor factorization and the localization universal property. For successive base changes, transpose both inverse comparisons under the final open adjunction. Both transposes are $G_{hg,V}\eta_j$ followed by the same iterated inverse-image compositor; naturality of the unit identifies the successive transpose with this one. For successive opens transpose under the composite open adjunction: the unit is $G_{j_1}\eta_{j_2}j_{1!}\circ\eta_{j_1}$, so again the two transposes coincide. Identity comparisons have the identity transpose. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijections proves the base-change, open-composition and identity laws, with the canonical compositors, before any evaluation. At finite $B$ this is the canonical extension-by-zero base change of the existing node, since its restriction comparison and open unit are the same ones.

proof.text: Construct $s$ by the fibre-product universal property. Base change of the open $i$ makes $b:W_S\to W$ an open immersion. The commutativity $pk=ir$ says that $k(V)$ lies in this open. Restricting an open immersion to an open containing its image is again the same isomorphism onto its image: identify $W_S$ with $p^{-1}(i(S))\subset W$, and $V$ with $k(V)$ therein; the induced map is $s$, by the fibre-product uniqueness. Thus $s$ is an open immersion, with $bs=k$ and $qs=r$. The map $q$ is separated, being the base change of the separated map $p$. Since $r$ is proper, the proper-over-separated theorem, applied over $S$ to $qs=r$, makes $s$ proper. A proper immersion is a closed immersion. Therefore $s(V)$ and its complement $C$ are disjoint open subschemes covering $W_S$. This argument applies equally to the empty open and does not assume that $r$ is an identity or that the original square is cartesian.

proof.text: For a module sheaf $F$ on $W_S$, every pro-etale test object $H$ is covered by the two disjoint opens $H\times_{W_S}s(V)$ and $H\times_{W_S}C$. The sheaf axiom identifies its sections with the product of the two component section modules, since the intersection is empty. Projection to the first factor, extended by zero on the second, consequently defines a unique natural module map $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$. On a clopen immersion extension by zero and direct image agree by exactly this product formula (the other component is the zero module); thus this is the claimed projection and it commutes with restrictions, module maps, tower transitions and differentials. Compose it with the $\beta$ of step 2 and the open-composition comparison to obtain exactly the displayed $\alpha_Q$. If the square is cartesian then $s=1$, so $\pi_s=1$ and $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$. If $r=1$ and $V=S$, then $s=(k,1)$ is the indicated clopen section and the projection is its component projection. This is a construction, not an inference from the finite-coefficient theorem.

proof.text:
We verify the geometric identities for $\alpha$ itself. Write $J_j=j_!$ and suppress inverse-image compositors. For vertically stacked squares the required identity is
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_{r_2})\circ(G_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2}):G_{p_1}G_{p_2}J_{i_2}\to J_{k_1}G_{r_1}G_{r_2}.$$
Use $\beta$ to identify the source with extension from the inverse image in the top-right scheme of the bottom-left open. The first projection on the right selects the inverse image of the middle-left open; the second selects the top-left open $k_1(V)$ inside it. The latter open is contained in the former by commutativity. Their composite is therefore identity on $k_1(V)$ and zero on the complementary clopen pieces, exactly the outer projection. To check this on sheaves, pull back the two clopen decompositions to each test object and take their four intersections; on each nonempty intersection the two maps are either both identity or both zero. Sheaf uniqueness then proves equality. For horizontally adjacent squares the formula is
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})\circ(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i):G_qJ_jJ_i\to J_lJ_kG_r.$$
Here the first projection selects $l(W)$ and the second selects $lk(V)$ inside it; the same intersection argument proves the formula. The $\beta$ and open-extension identifications agree by step 2, so these are identities of the specified maps, not just their supports. Finally base change pulls $W_S=s(V)\amalg C$ to $W_{1,S_1}=s_1(V_1)\amalg C_1$. Inverse image sends this split module decomposition and its identity/zero projections to the pulled-back ones, since it is additive and preserves finite products. The beta comparisons identify the two open extensions by step 2. If $\theta:G_{p_1}G_b\cong G_aG_p$ is the pullback square identification, the resulting cube equation is
$$(\beta_kG_r)\circ(G_a\alpha_Q)\circ(\theta J_i)=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_c)\circ(G_{p_1}\beta_i),$$
where $G_dG_r$ and $G_{r_1}G_c$ are identified canonically. It is checked on the two clopen components just described. These arguments work on arbitrary sheaves and with arbitrary $B$.

proof.text:
All functors occurring in $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are exact. Apply their sheaf transformations termwise to towers and then to complexes. Exact-functor factorization and the uniqueness part of localization descend their transformations and every equation of steps 2, 4 and 5 to the unbounded derived strict-tower categories. Now take the mate of $\alpha_Q$ for $G_r\dashv R_r^{\mathcal T}$ and $G_p\dashv R_p^{\mathcal T}$. The mate definition is precisely
$$(R_p^{\mathcal T}J_k\varepsilon_r)\circ(R_p^{\mathcal T}\alpha_QR_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\eta_pJ_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
This constructs the stated $\gamma_Q$, naturally on the derived tower category. Its transformation is fixed by this formula on that category. In particular it is not selected by asking for prescribed evaluations.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), unit-square-counit construction; arbitrary proper/open square uses alpha from steps 4-5

proof.text: Evaluation commutes with exact $G_u,J_j$ termwise. Choose a K-injective tower representative $I$ of an input. Its evaluation $I_n$ is K-injective by the tower-evaluation theorem, so $\operatorname{ev}_n(u_*I)=u_*I_n$ computes both $\operatorname{ev}_nR_u^{\mathcal T}$ and $Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n$, with the canonical resolution comparison. These identifications preserve the adjunction units and counits: on homotopy categories the adjunction is the termwise one, and the canonical derived Hom bijection is computed by that adjunction into the K-injective representative. Evaluating that chain-map transpose gives exactly the transpose into $I_n$; the K-injective Hom bijection makes it the same derived transpose. Hence evaluating the mate formula of step 6 gives the single-level mate of the single-level clopen $\alpha_Q$. No assertion that evaluation is faithful is needed. For a coefficient map $B\to\Lambda$, apply the ring-sheaf-change-adjunction theorem to $\underline B_T\to\underline\Lambda_T$. It supplies the canonical inverse-image and derived direct-image scalar-restriction comparisons and their adjunct identity. Open extension commutes with scalar restriction as well: its extension presheaf has exactly the same underlying additive sections and the restricted scalar action, and sheafification gives the same underlying sheaf with that action. The component projection also has the same identity/zero formula. Thus the adjunct identity and the mate formula identify the single-level $B$-mate on $\operatorname{Res}N$ with the restriction of the $\Lambda$-mate on $N$. This uses no flatness of $B\to\Lambda$ and does not assert that scalar restriction preserves K-injectives.

proof.text:
We identify the resulting single-level mate at $
u_V^*L$, for finite $\Lambda$ and $L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. First the normalized finite etale comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] is the mate of the etale version of our $\alpha$. To see the normalization, restrict to $i:S\hookrightarrow T$. Localization gives $G_iRp_*k_!L\cong Rq_*G_bk_!L=Rq_*s_!L\cong Rr_*L$. The last comparison uses $s_!=s_*$ for the clopen component and derived pushforward composition. On a K-injective representative $J$ of $L$, the sheaf identification $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J$ in that node restricts, under these identifications, to the identity of $r_*J$: sections on $s(V)$ are retained and the complementary component is zero. A resolution $k_!J	o I$ gives the canonical derived comparison, so the open-adjunction transpose of that node's specified arrow is the inverse of this restriction identification. The transpose of our proper mate is the same map: restricting $\alpha$ to $s(V)$ gives the identity and $G_rRr_*	o1$ is its counit, so the proper adjunction triangle identity cancels its unit. Injectivity of the open-adjunction Hom bijection identifies the two arrows. This also proves the claimed refinement normalization, since the finite node explicitly identifies its refinement arrow.
Now compare the two sites. The finite open comparison $
u^*j_!\cong j_!
u^*$ and pullback comparison identify the two alpha maps: after the clopen decomposition each is identity on the same component and zero on its complement. The canonical direct-image comparison is explicitly the counit mate in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Its displayed counit equation, applied to $p$ and $r$, and the mate-pasting identities therefore identify the proper mate of this alpha square with
$$i_!
u_S^*Rr_{\mathrm{et},*}L\cong
u_T^*i_!Rr_{\mathrm{et},*}L\xrightarrow{
u_T^*\gamma_Q^{\mathrm{et}}}
u_T^*Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}k_!L\cong Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}k_!
u_V^*L,$$
with the source also identified with $i_!Rr_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_V^*L$. More explicitly, transpose under $G_p\dashv Rp_*$: the counit equation replaces $G_p$ of each direct-image comparison followed by $\varepsilon_p$ by $
u^*\varepsilon_p^{\mathrm{et}}$; the same equation for $r$ replaces its counit. The remaining map is precisely the compared clopen alpha, so the two transposes are equal. Proper $p,r$ are qcqs: finite type includes quasi-compactness, and their separated diagonals are closed immersions. On an affine open a closed immersion is the affine quotient by an ideal, so its inverse image is quasi-compact. Thus the diagonals are quasi-compact, which is the definition of quasi-separatedness. These are exactly the hypotheses of the direct-image site-comparison theorem; no Noetherian hypothesis on schemes is used. Exact open extension preserves the lower bound of $L$, so $k_!L$ is also in its required $D^+$ domain. The displayed transported comparison is an isomorphism because the finite etale gamma and the two canonical site comparisons are isomorphisms. Together with step 7 this proves both the specified finite-evaluation normalization and invertibility of every evaluated gamma in the statement.

proof.text: Let $M$ satisfy the stated witnesses, with a possibly different finite ring and lower bound for every $n$. Step 7 transports evaluation of $\gamma_{Q,M}$ along the given isomorphism $\operatorname{ev}_nM\cong\operatorname{Res}\nu_V^*L_n$; step 8 proves that transported arrow is an isomorphism. Evaluation is exact and tower cohomology is levelwise, so for every degree $a$ the morphism $H^a(\gamma_{Q,M})$ has isomorphic components at every $n$. A morphism of towers with isomorphic components is itself invertible: the component inverses commute with transitions by multiplying the original commutative transition squares by those inverses. Therefore each $H^a(\gamma_{Q,M})$ is an isomorphism, and the unbounded-derived cohomology criterion makes $\gamma_{Q,M}$ an isomorphism. This detects invertibility only. It does not infer equality of derived morphisms from equality of their evaluations, and it uses no uniform bound in $n$.

proof.text:
Apply the two mate-pasting formulas to the alpha equations in step 5, now in the derived tower categories of step 6. Pasting along the proper adjunctions sends $(\alpha_{Q_1}G_{r_2})(G_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2})$ to
$$(R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}R_{r_1}^{\mathcal T}).$$
Pasting along the open functors sends $(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i)$ to
$$(\gamma_{Q_2}J_k)\circ(J_j\gamma_{Q_1}).$$
These are the two displayed gamma laws. Use the composite-adjunction units and counits in the mate-pasting theorem. They correspond to the canonical proper direct-image compositor: right adjoints of the exact inverse images preserve K-injectives, so on a K-injective tower complex $I$ the composition is represented by the underived equality $(p_2p_1)_*I=p_{2,*}p_{1,*}I$; this is the normalization of the ringed-topos composition theorem on the diagram sites. The open compositor is similarly the unit-normalized left adjoint of iterated restriction from step 2. For three proper maps, these underived identifications associate to the same triple direct image on $I$; for three opens the transposes are the same iterated restriction unit. The Hom/localization bijections and uniqueness of adjoints preserve these equations. Together with associativity of natural-transformation composition and the alpha projection identities, this proves independence of parenthesization. Identity horizontal maps give $\alpha=1_{G_p}$ and the identity clause of mate-pasting gives $1_{R_p^{\mathcal T}}$. Identity vertical maps give $\alpha=1_{J_i}$ and identity adjunctions give $1_{J_i}$. These are equalities of derived tower transformations on all inputs, before the finite-origin restriction.

proof.text:
Finally take mates of the cube equation in step 5. The pullback square isomorphisms $G_{p_1}G_b\cong G_aG_p$ and $G_{r_1}G_c\cong G_dG_r$ have mates $E_p^{\mathcal T}$ and $E_r^{\mathcal T}$. The mate-pasting formulas, with the open beta transformations left untransposed, turn the left side of that cube into
$$(R_{p_1}^{\mathcal T}\beta_k)\circ(E_p^{\mathcal T}J_k)\circ(G_b\gamma_Q),$$
and the right side into
$$(\gamma_{Q_1}G_d)\circ(J_{i_1}E_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\beta_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
One can verify the cancellations directly from the mate formula: insert $\eta_p,\varepsilon_r$ for $\gamma_Q$ and the analogous units and counits for the two exchange mates; naturality moves the beta and alpha factors between them. Each intermediate adjacent unit-counit pair cancels by the adjunction triangle identity. The two uncancelled middle composites are exactly $(\beta_kG_r)(G_a\alpha_Q)(\theta J_i)$ and $(\alpha_{Q_1}G_c)(G_{p_1}\beta_i)$ of step 5, so their equality proves this formula. This uses the mate-pasting theorem as an equality theorem, not invertibility of either exchange. Proper and open base-change stability ensure that $Q_1$ is again an allowed square, and quasi-compactness of the opens is preserved by base change. All constituent equations were already descended from strict sheaf-diagram equations or proved by adjunction in the strict derived categories. Thus the base-change equation, the two composition laws and their identity normalizations hold for arbitrary commutative proper/open squares, including all intermediate refinement squares specified in the statement.
